FN-9E49MBB-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 278
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Representative Susan DuBose
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/09/2024
House Bill 278 as introduced would increase the obligations of the local boards of education by
an undetermined amount beginning with the 2025-2026 school year by allowing home-schooled
students to participate in career and technical programs in public schools dependent upon the
cost of any required increase in instructional personnel and/or classroom space to accommodate
the additional such students. This increase in obligations may be offset, in whole or in part, by
the collection of course fees from the student equal to the fee charged to an enrolled public
school student.
Additionally, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of the State Board of
Education and the local school boards of education to adopt rules and policies, respectively,
pursuant to this bill.

FN-9E49MBB-3
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 278
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Representative Susan DuBose
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 05/01/2024
House Bill 278 as passed the House of Representatives would increase the obligations of the
local boards of education, beginning with the 2025-2026 school year, by allowing
home-schooled students to participate in career and technical programs in public schools. The
increase in obligations would be dependent upon the cost of any required increase in
instructional personnel and/or classroom space to accommodate the additional students, and
could be offset, in whole or in part, by the collection of course fees received from the student
equal to the fee charged to an enrolled public school student.
Additionally, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of the State Board of
Education and the local school boards of education to adopt rules and policies, respectively,
pursuant to this bill.
